clue.text: Keep my French polish in a tin

indicators.note: to polish something is to work it over and refine it, so the following letters are reworked

parts.note: ma is the French feminine form of 'my'
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to store one's French furniture polish in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' reads as a noun being kept in a tin, but it is the verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it up or preserve it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Each day enthralled by cut grass on field

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive, so these pieces are held within the next one

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
ea. is the abbreviation for each
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Every day someone is captivated by mown grass in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a field of grass, often kept for hay.

clue.text: One minute before person in theatre potentially gets irritated

parts.note: Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for minute
someone in an operating theatre is probably having surgery

explanation.surface: A theatregoer gets annoyed one minute before the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the hospital operating theatre, not a playhouse; 'before' puts one and minute ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient means restless and annoyed at delay, close to irritated.

clue.text: Spiny plant ripped trousers horribly at first

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the word before takes in what follows

parts.note: ripped means torn

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of horribly

explanation.surface: Torn trousers from a nasty spiky bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' reads as a noun after ripped, but it is the verb to trouser, meaning pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn, such as hawthorn, is a prickly shrub or tree.

clue.text: Bend in crow's head and crow's foot

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of the word it belongs to

parts.note: first letter of crow
a crow's foot is a wrinkle at the corner of the eye

explanation.surface: A kink in a bird's head and foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Crow's feet are wrinkles beside the eyes; a wrinkle is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To incline is to lean or bow, so to bend.

clue.text: City greatly encapsulating Northern Ireland

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing as in a capsule, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: much means to a great degree
standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A city that greatly embraces Northern Ireland, perhaps in its sporting ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich is the Bavarian capital in southern Germany, an example of a city.

clue.text: Boxers perhaps lower energy in fight

parts.note: under means lower

indicators.note: in places the energy symbol inside the word for fight

parts.note: a war is a fight
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Pugilists perhaps losing energy in a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' suggests fighters, and fight backs that up, but they are boxer shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are an example of underwear, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Angry thief in the main wanting power

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the thief's word goes without that letter

parts.note: the main is the open sea, where pirates steal
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A furious robber who is mostly lacking any power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, a direct synonym.

clue.text: The chap's scoffed after IT delay

parts.note: he's, the chap is
taken as written
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A man has eaten after an IT outage held things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After IT' places the word for scoffed after IT; IT looks like information technology but is just the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause or hold back before acting, so to delay.

clue.text: Advance very quietly and fish move closer

parts.note: A is used as an abbreviation for advance(d), as in A level
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Stalking advice for an angler: creep up very quietly on the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' looks like the definition, but it supplies only its abbreviation; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to come nearer to something, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Higher standards from international agreements

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for international
deals are agreements

explanation.surface: Raising the bar through international trade agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are principles or standards of perfection one aims at, hence higher standards.

clue.text: Husband in terrific pain

indicators.note: in puts the husband abbreviation inside the word for terrific

parts.note: ace means excellent
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A spouse in dreadful agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrific' suggests terrible here, but it means first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a continuous dull pain.

clue.text: New backing protects this newspaper on many occasions

indicators.note: something that protects surrounds and shields what it guards
backing means going backwards, so the word for new is read from its end

parts.note: neo- is the prefix meaning new
the Financial Times, where this puzzle appears

explanation.surface: A new financial backer protects the paper time and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This newspaper' is the FT because the crossword is printed in the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, that is, happening on many occasions.

clue.text: I note chapter rector translated is not accurate

indicators.note: translating changes a text into another form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
first letter of note
C is the abbreviation for chapter
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots an error in how a rector's chapter was translated.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation of note here too; take it as the first letter if the abbreviation is unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect means wrong, a direct synonym of not accurate.

clue.text: Group left game finally fit

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word just before it

parts.note: last letter of game
an ague is a feverish fit of shivering

explanation.surface: A sports team pulls out of a match, eventually fit again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective meaning healthy; here it is a noun, a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an association or group, of clubs or of allied nations.

clue.text: Easel girl assembled for art exhibition rooms

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so these letters are built up in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A young woman sets up an easel for a show in a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleries are rooms or buildings where art is displayed.

clue.text: Bit inside ukelele men twanged

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A snippet played by men strumming ukuleles.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component or part of a whole, so a bit.

clue.text: Remove knotted tie in meal

indicators.note: knotted means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Taking off a tie that got knotted at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to get rid of or remove.

clue.text: Puts up with spare tyres

definitions.meaning: second meaning: bellies, a spare tyre being a roll of fat round the middle

explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is jokey slang for a paunch, not a car part.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate it, and stomachs are also bellies or paunches.

clue.text: Clean child with friend

parts.note: a tot is a small child
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A child who gets washed together with a playmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean' looks like a verb or adjective for washing; it is the adverb, as in 'I clean forgot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, clean means completely, as in clean forgot, matching the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Some Chicago youths turned up for spiritual discipline

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
some means a part of the following words, so the letters lie within them

parts.note: the letters spanning these two words

explanation.surface: Some young people in Chicago showed up for a spiritual practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is the Hindu discipline of meditation and posture aimed at spiritual union.

clue.text: Druggie regularly seen in bloke's room

indicators.note: seen in places the selected letters inside the following word

parts.note: a bloke is a man

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A drug user keeps turning up in some fellow's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room' is not a chamber but space to spare, as in room for error.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is spare space or leeway, the sense of room in 'room for manoeuvre'.

clue.text: Sort of swallow current drink

parts.note: martins are birds of the swallow family
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Instructions to knock back a fresh drink in one swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' is the bird, not a gulp.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka and vermouth.

clue.text: Invented Edam?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in a down entry, a word written upwards; Edam is a four-letter word reversed

explanation.walkthrough: Edam is a Dutch cheese, but read bottom to top it spells a word for created; the answer describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Made up means invented or fictitious, and also literally describes a word written upward.

clue.text: Miles west of German city with German emissary

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for miles
Essen is a city in the Ruhr
Ger. is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Directions: a place a few miles west of a German city, with a German envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, west of means placed to the left, so the miles come first.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is someone sent with a message, which is what a messenger is.

clue.text: Scrape spades on sock

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
to sock or cuff someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: Scraping spades on a sock while digging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sock' looks like footwear; it means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuff is to scrape or mark a surface by rubbing.

clue.text: Tea bags in high quality porcelain

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a sack, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tea bags kept in a fine porcelain caddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea bags' reads as a noun phrase, but bags is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine vitreous ceramic ware, porcelain of high quality originally from China.

clue.text: Canine by George's hamper

parts.note: C is the dental shorthand for a canine tooth
both are mild exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A dog belonging to George has a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket; it is the verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To check is to restrain or impede, the same as to hamper.

clue.text: Relative calm, initially, by old American home

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of calm
O is the abbreviation for old
US for American
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A family member stays calm at first beside an old American house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative calm' reads as a phrase; the comma splits it into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a child of one's aunt or uncle, so a kind of relative.

clue.text: Free lino with 50% off carpet

indicators.note: 50% off leaves half of the word, here the front half

parts.note: the first half of lino
to carpet someone is to give them a telling-off

explanation.surface: A sale ad: free lino with half off a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb, to reprimand, as when a worker is called on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set free, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Most sound from son before a party

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
a fest is a festive gathering

explanation.surface: The loudest noise comes from a son heading off to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' suggests noise; it means secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe means secure or sound, so the superlative safest is most sound.

clue.text: This writer at university is after finest refreshing drink

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the finest
the setter refers to themself
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: The setter, a student, follows the best with a restorative drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the setter and university after the word for finest. Being up is the British idiom for being in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up is a tonic or stimulating drink that revives you.
